title: Interest Rate Futures: Eurodollar Futures, Convexity, and Duration Hedging
targetAudiencePersona: Fixed Income Portfolio Manager & Bank Risk Officer
prerequisites: Treasury bond futures and conversion factor mechanics from Chapter 6 Part 1
Yield to maturity and continuous compounding from Chapter 4
Cost of carry forward pricing parity from Chapter 5
learningOutcomes: Interpret Eurodollar and SOFR 3-month futures quotes and calculate dollar gains per basis point.
Calculate the convexity adjustment between interest rate futures and forward borrowing rates.
Calculate Macaulay duration and modified duration to estimate linear bond price sensitivity.
Analyze second-order convexity curvature protection against large macro yield shifts.
Size optimal duration hedges using N* = (P * D_P) / (V_F * D_F) to immunize balance sheets.
Diagnose commercial bank asset-liability duration gaps and explain insolvency risk (Snapshot 6.3).

sections.title: Bank ALM Duration Crisis & Insolvency Mechanics
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Demonstrate how unhedged duration gaps destroy bank equity capital during rate hike cycles.
keyPoints: Banks fund long-duration assets (7-yr mortgages) with short-duration liabilities (1-yr deposits).
A +200 bps yield surge causes a -$140M loss on assets and an $18M gain on liabilities.
Net equity deficit of -$122M completely wipes out the bank's $100M capital base (Snapshot 6.3).
sections.formulaUsed: Delta E = -(D_A * A - D_L * L) * Delta y

sections.title: Eurodollar & SOFR 3-Month Futures Architecture
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Establish contract specifications, Price = 100 - R quoting, and the $25 per tick invariant.
keyPoints: Contract covers $1,000,000 principal of 3-month deposits referencing short-term rates.
Price is quoted on an index basis: Price = 100 - R (e.g., 4.5% rate quotes at 95.50).
Every 1 basis point (0.01%) rate move is worth exactly $25 cash per contract.

sections.title: Futures vs Forward Rates: The Convexity Adjustment
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Derive the convexity adjustment formula and explain why futures rates exceed forward rates.
keyPoints: Daily mark-to-market settlement induces positive correlation with interest rates.
Futures rates systematically exceed theoretical forward rates for long maturities.
Subtracting 0.5 * sigma^2 * T1 * T2 yields the true forward borrowing rate.
sections.formulaUsed: Forward Rate = Futures Rate - 0.5 * sigma^2 * T1 * T2

sections.title: Macaulay Duration & Modified Duration
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Formulate Macaulay duration as cash flow timing and Modified duration as linear price sensitivity.
keyPoints: Macaulay duration measures weighted average maturity of discounted coupon and principal cash flows.
Modified duration D* dictates linear price sensitivity: Delta B / B approx -D* * Delta y.
Negative sign reflects the fundamental inverse relationship between bond prices and interest rates.
sections.formulaUsed: Delta B / B approx -D* * Delta y

sections.title: Convexity Protection & The Master Duration Hedge Ratio
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Formulate second-order convexity curvature and derive the optimal hedge ratio N*.
keyPoints: Convexity ensures bond prices rise faster on yield drops than they fall on yield hikes.
Immunize portfolios by shorting N* = (P * D_P) / (V_F * D_F) futures contracts.
Worked example: Shorting 423 contracts immunizes a $50M portfolio with duration 6.8 years.

misconceptions.misconception: Futures interest rates and forward interest rates are always identical for the same maturity.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Daily mark-to-market settlement creates covariance between rate levels and reinvestment, causing futures rates to systematically exceed forward rates by the convexity adjustment.

misconceptions.misconception: A bond's maturity in calendar years is the correct measure of its price sensitivity to interest rate shifts.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Coupons paid before maturity shorten effective cash flow timing; modified duration—not maturity—measures true interest rate price sensitivity.

misconceptions.misconception: Duration-based hedging insulates bond portfolios against all types of interest rate risks.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Standard duration hedging assumes small parallel shifts of the yield curve; non-parallel twists, steepening, and credit basis risk leave residual exposure.

activeRecallQuiz.scenario: A commercial bank holds a $50M corporate bond portfolio with modified duration 6.8 years. Treasury bond futures have price $98,000 and the cheapest-to-deliver bond has modified duration 8.2 years.
activeRecallQuiz.question: How many futures contracts must the portfolio manager short to immunize the portfolio against parallel yield curve shifts?
activeRecallQuiz.explanation: Applying N* = (P * D_P) / (V_F * D_F) yields (50,000,000 * 6.8) / (98,000 * 8.2) = 340,000,000 / 803,600 = 423.1 contracts. Shorting 423 contracts immunizes the portfolio.

coreTakeaways: Eurodollar and SOFR 3-month futures quote as 100 - R, with a standard $25 tick value per basis point.
The convexity adjustment reduces long-dated futures rates to obtain true forward borrowing rates.
Modified duration provides the first-order linear price loss metric: Delta B / B approx -D* * Delta y.
Positive convexity acts as embedded curvature protection, dampening price drops and magnifying gains.
Unhedged bank duration gaps cause catastrophic balance sheet insolvency during sharp rate hiking cycles.
Shorting N* = (P * D_P) / (V_F * D_F) contracts provides mathematical portfolio immunization.
